context:
When a picture is more than four times as tall as it is wide (a long page, more than 1560 px high for a 390 px wide drawing), the 480 px height cap would squeeze it into a thin strip. As built, a floor stops that: the picture never goes narrower than 120 px, so it can run past 480 px high. The other way is no floor, so the cap always wins.

Correction: an earlier note called this a minimum height. It is a minimum width (page.html reads `a capped picture is never narrower than this, however tall the mockup`). Reversible, and the pictures below show a 390 by 2400 drawing both ways.

options.gain: A tall picture stays wide enough to see.
options.how:
A very tall picture stays 120 px wide and may be taller than 480 px.
Before: a thin strip. After: 120 by 738 for a 390 by 2400 drawing.
options.label: Keep the 120 px minimum width (as built)
options.lose: That card is taller than 480 px, so one tall picture makes its row taller.

options.gain: No card is ever taller than the cap.
options.how:
A very tall picture is cut down to 480 px high and becomes narrow.
Before: 120 wide. After: 78 by 480 for a 390 by 2400 drawing.
options.label: No minimum: the 480 px cap always wins
options.lose: A tall picture becomes a thin strip that is hard to see.

ref: c193 (waiting page: pictures and chips fit), PR #783; the floor is MIN_PIC in skills/waiting-page/page.html
reply: Answered, Oct 28 17:50 CDT: the 120 px minimum width stays (a). Your note asks two things. (1) Zoom to the area that needs review: the page already does this when a mockup names a focus element; the card then shows that element, fitted to the card. (2) Scroll inside the picture when it is bigger than its box: the card picture does not scroll today (it is clipped, and a tap opens the full-size sheet, which does scroll). I filed (2) on c193 as a new want, to be scoped after the sizes PR (#783) merges.
title: Should a very tall picture keep a minimum width of 120 px?
why: A picture too thin to see does no good in a card, and the case is rare; it ships as built unless you say otherwise.
